events.title: Dartmouth AI summer research proposal
events.summary: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester, and Claude Shannon submitted their Dartmouth proposal on August 31, 1955 — the document that coined the term [artificial intelligence].
events.about: The four-page proposal requested funding for a 1956 summer study on making machines learn, use language, and solve human-level problems. McCarthy invented the phrase '[artificial intelligence]' for the grant application; the workshop it launched became the field's founding event.

narrative.whyChosen: This proposal named the field and framed AI as an engineering summer project.
narrative.whyImportant: It united logic, neuroscience, and computing under one research agenda.
narrative.problemSolved: [Machine learning] and reasoning research lacked a shared name, goal, and funding pitch.

events.title: Dartmouth proposal: simulate every feature of intelligence
events.quoteText: The study is to proceed on the basis of the conjecture that every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it.
events.summary: The 1955 Dartmouth grant proposal states the founding conjecture of AI — that intelligence can be precisely described enough for machines to simulate it.
events.about: This sentence is the mission statement behind decades of AI research, from symbolic [expert system]s to [deep learning]. It assumes intelligence is describable in rules and representations — a bet the field is still testing.

narrative.whyChosen: The conjecture that launched [artificial intelligence] as a named discipline.
narrative.whyImportant: It reframed cognition as an engineering specification problem.
narrative.problemSolved: Researchers in logic, psychology, and computing had no shared hypothesis to organize collaborative work.
